core_conclusion: Show the actual Forest reconstruction's validated reliability, cost, and runtime while making incomplete original-artifact coverage visible; do not imply replication of 17.1x or 100% reliability.
archetype: quantitative grid with a geometry example
backend: Python/matplotlib, matching the existing Python experiment workflow

panels: A: lexicographically first frozen Forest case with all 15 obstacles and saved candidate paths
B: independent validation pass counts over the full requested denominator
C: actual distance-problem runtime distributions, all recorded attempts
D: actual time-problem runtime distributions, all recorded attempts

figure_2.purpose: show every case's result and failures without selecting favourable seeds
figure_2.layout: one status heatmap per method, environment seed by roadmap seed/node count

selection.quantitative: all requested cases and methods; absent outputs retained as not_run
selection.geometry_example: lexicographically first case, an illustration only; not selected by outcome

uncertainty: main figures are full observed ECDFs and full-denominator proportions; report empirical SD and environment-clustered bootstrap intervals in tables, no iid significance claim over repeated seeds
risk_checks: published values kept in reference-only table
Franka and KUKA are marked unavailable rather than replaced by Kinova
solver success separated from independent collision validation
paired costs only on common validated successes
no discarded timeouts or solver errors
